```markdown
# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md; ranking and track confirmed in your partner's words, 2026-11-10. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
Choices made: uv workspace with four package scaffolds; the spec places the code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` (§4.9).
Choices made: Azure platform per the ADR, status Proposed; its acceptance is §7 step 1.

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a configured range, downloaded and kept | §3 R1; §2.1, §4.2 | A | 1 | Bytes and time per quarter: measured by Stage 1. Requests: about one listing plus one file per quarter (§4.2), so the 3 req/s target (§4.8) is not the constraint. Full volume: per-quarter bytes × quarters in the range, and the range is not yet set (§4.8). |
| O2 | Daily indexes picked up on an ongoing basis, including catch-up after missed runs | §3 R2; §4.2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year (business days), each one listing plus one file. Per-file size: measured by Stage 1. |
| O3 | A normalized filing-index dataset in Parquet, built from the downloaded indexes | §3 R3; §4.5, §4.6 | A | 3 | Compute per quarter (elapsed time, peak memory): measured by Stage 1. |
| O4 | The ingestion running on Azure: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Azure Monitor | §3 R4; §4.1, §4.9 | A | 4 | Monthly Azure cost: cannot be estimated without deploying; measured by Stage 7's smoke test (§7 step 4). §2.2 excludes a cost guarantee before measurement. |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs sharing one downloader, parser and publisher | §3 R5; §4.1 | A | 5 | No external cost; your partner's time only. |
| O6 | Stored original bytes reprocessed after a parser change, with no new download | §3 R6; §4.3, §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage: raw bytes once per distinct snapshot. A replay makes 0 SEC requests (§4.3). |
| O7 | Periodic re-reading of quarterly indexes, with additions and field changes recorded | §3 R7; §4.2, §4.4 | A | 7 | Each weekly run re-reads every supported quarter (§4.8). About 2 requests per quarter, so about 70 s of requests per 100 quarters at 3 req/s. Bytes are about the full baseline volume per run. |
| O8 | All SEC traffic under one request budget, however many workers run | §3 R8; §4.3 | A | 8 | None material. |
| O9 | Readers get a complete, versioned quarter through one active pointer | §3 R9; §4.5, §4.6 | A | 9 | About one quarter's Parquet per generation, multiplied by retained generations. Retention is not yet set (§4.8). |
| O10 | Records removed from a closed quarter leave the catalog only after hash-bound approval | §3 R10; §4.4 | A | 10 | Your partner's time per gated withdrawal. Frequency is unknown until reconciliation runs (Stage 6). |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and rate target held as reviewed configuration defaults | §3 R11; §4.8 | A | 11 | None material. |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

Order follows dependency, not the rank above. Three stages move ahead of their rank:

- The request budget and configuration (O8, O11) come before any multi-file SEC traffic.
- Raw snapshots and the manifest (O6) come before backfill, so that backfill keeps replayable inputs.
- Azure (O4) comes after the local contracts it hosts are built.

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter and one real day, end to end, locally
      Objective: Fetch one archived quarterly and one published daily master index from the SEC, and write their rows to the canonical row contract in local Parquet.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: the generated workspace scaffolds; an SEC User-Agent identity supplied by your partner (§4.8)
      Produces: a parser and normalizer for the sec-index-v1 row contract; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one archived quarter's master.idx is fetched with an identifying User-Agent at or below 3 req/s, and kept with its SHA-256. O3 — that quarter's rows and one daily index's rows are in sec-index-v1 Parquet; the row count matches the data lines; malformed rows are refused, not dropped. Cost — the findings file records, for the real run: bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, request count and observed request rate.
      Leaves out: shared lease and retry policy (Stage 2); config validation (Stage 2); manifest and replay (Stage 3); range and daily discovery (Stage 4); generations and active pointer (Stage 5); Azure deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: One request budget and validated configuration
      Objective: Route every SEC request through one throttled, lease-held collector, configured by validated settings.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stage 1's fetch path
      Produces: a single SEC access path with lease, throttle, bounded retries and halt on access denial; typed configuration validated before any I/O
      Exit: O8 — CI shows concurrent collectors sharing one budget; retries count toward it; lease loss and takeover create no overlapping request issuers; Retry-After is honored; access denial halts SEC access (§6 Access). O11 — every §4.8 key is loaded and validated; each §5 Configuration case is refused before external I/O.
      Leaves out: Azure Storage-backed lease (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Raw snapshots, source manifest and replay
      Objective: Keep content-addressed original bytes and manifest records, so transforms replay from storage alone.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stage 1's parser; Stage 2's access path
      Produces: the raw and observations layouts (§4.5); Source, Snapshot, Workset-binding, Processing and Attempt records; quarantine handling
      Exit: O6 — CI shows a parser-version change rebuilding observations from raw storage with zero SEC requests; unchanged hashes skip work; repeated inputs give the same logical rows (§6 Replay).
      Leaves out: Table Storage and ADLS backing (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Backfill and daily discovery on shared workflows
      Objective: Discover and ingest a quarter range and daily indexes through one discover/collect/transform command set, with source-file checkpoints.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O5
      Consumes: Stages 2 and 3
      Produces: the `discover`, `collect` and `transform` commands; immutable worksets; run reports with gaps and pending sources
      Exit: O1 — a configured quarter range is ingested and reported as complete, pending or failed per unit. O2 — CI covers missed runs, outages across quarters, valid empty listings and failed listings that do not advance the boundary (§6 Discovery). O5 — backfill and daily differ only in source selection: one downloader, one parser.
      Leaves out: publication and the `publish` command (Stage 5); ADF scheduling (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Versioned quarter generations and active pointer
      Objective: Publish each affected quarter as a complete generation behind a conditionally replaced pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 4's observations and run reports
      Produces: the `publish` command; generation manifests and change reports; the Quarter-publication record
      Exit: O9 — CI shows crash injection before files finish, before the pointer update and after it; readers see only complete generations; competing publishers lose no update (§6 Publication).
      Leaves out: withdrawal gate (Stage 6); Table Storage conditional writes on Azure (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and the withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly sources and apply §4.4 precedence, publishing safe changes and gating removals.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 5
      Produces: the reconciliation workflow; Withdrawal-approval records; the `awaiting_approval` outcome
      Exit: O7 — additions and field updates are recorded with provenance. O10 — CI shows open-quarter absence never withdraws; closed-quarter removal needs approval bound to the exact source hash; stale daily replay cannot resurrect a withdrawn key (§6 Reconciliation).
      Leaves out: scheduled weekly trigger (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment, integration tests and smoke test
      Objective: Host the shared worker on Azure per the accepted ADR, and pass §7 Phase 1 steps 1–5.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 2–6; ADR acceptance (§7 step 1)
      Produces: infra under version control (§4.9); ADF pipelines with triggers disabled; managed identities; Storage-backed lease and pointer; structured logs and alerts (§4.7); smoke-test record
      Exit: O4 — integration tests on isolated Azure resources pass (§6 Orchestration, Observability, and Integration tests). A bounded live smoke test of one quarter and one daily index records bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest and request rate. A raw-storage replay with SEC access disabled shows no duplicates.
      Leaves out: production backfill, trigger enablement and runbooks (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Baseline campaign and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run §7 Phase 2: production backfill, daily catch-up, first reconciliation, trigger enablement and runbooks.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7
      Consumes: Stage 7
      Produces: the published baseline; enabled triggers; runbooks (§8); a release record
      Exit: O1 — every requested unit is published, or the incomplete range is recorded and approved. O2 — the daily trigger is enabled after the catch-up result is accepted, and observed scheduled runs match their reports. O7 — the manual reconciliation resolved its gated candidates, and the weekly trigger is enabled.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run SKILL.md §6 over O1–O11, with evidence per verdict: the implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, and deferred items. R1–R11 are each cited by an outcome's Spec cell. Each unmet outcome exits as a new stage, or as a deferral with a written why.
```
